instructions: Heat the broiler and set a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil. Cut the poblanos in half, remove the stems and seeds, and set them skin side up on the sheet. Broil for 6 to 8 minutes, turning the sheet halfway, until the skins are well charred.
Meanwhile, slice each chicken breast in half horizontally into 2 thin cutlets. Pat them dry and season with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Halve and slice the onions 1/4 inch thick.
Transfer the hot poblanos to a bowl and cover it with a plate. Let them steam for 5 minutes.

While they steam, heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the cutlets in two batches, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden. They won't be cooked through yet. Transfer them to a plate.
Peel the skins off the poblanos. Don't rinse them. Slice the peppers into 1/4-inch strips.

Turn the heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the onions and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for about 5 minutes, until the onions are soft and lightly browned. Mince the garlic, add it with the poblano strips and the last 1/4 tsp salt, and cook for 1 minute.

Pour in the crema and bring it to a boil. Nestle the cutlets and any juices from the plate into the sauce. Turn the heat to medium-low, cover and cook for 5 to 6 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece. It's done when there's no pink left.
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and let it rest for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, cook the sauce over medium heat for 2 to 4 minutes, until a spatula pulled through it leaves a clear trail.
Take the pan off the heat. Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro and stir it in with a squeeze of the lime. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Slice the chicken across the grain and serve it with the rajas and the sauce.
method_notes: Lead is America's Test Kitchen's chicken with rajas (4.5 from 19 ratings, one short of the 20 needed, so a fallback lead). It is a cream dish: the crema is what the sauce is built on, in this and in every other version read (Dish n the Kitchen and Food.com also use crema, cream cheese or sour cream). Because crema defines the dish, the dairy-free tag is dropped. The lead's whole breasts are cut into cutlets so the chicken cooks in 5 to 6 minutes in the sauce and the dish fits about 45 minutes; the broiler charring and steaming of the poblanos is unchanged.
